quests.instruction: Choose the best revision of the unclear claim.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Lockers are a thing that schools could do something about.'
options: Lockers exist in many schools across the country and beyond.
Schools should provide lockers so students do not carry heavy bags all day.
Schools could maybe think about lockers in some kinds of situations.
Lockers are important for schools and for students in many ways.
quests.hint: A clear claim says what should happen and why.
quests.explanation: The right revision states the action and the reason. The alternatives are vague or only describe.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The chat app situation at work needs looking at.'
options: The chat app situation could be improved in some ways, perhaps after the team has discussed the matter further.
The chat app is a problem that people should look at fairly soon, before it causes any further difficulty.
Our team should move project updates from the chat app into a weekly email, because important messages are getting lost.
Chat apps at work have both good sides and bad sides, and the team should think about both of them.
quests.hint: Turn 'needs looking at' into a specific recommendation.
quests.explanation: The correct revision names the change and the reason. The rest still avoid a position.

quests.instruction: Choose the clearest and most specific claim.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Delivery fees are unfair.'
options: Delivery fees should be shown before checkout, because surprise charges make orders cost more than customers expect.
Delivery fees are a big problem for a lot of people these days, and something ought to be done about them.
Delivery fees are unfair to customers in various different respects, and they should be reviewed by the company.
Delivery fees are not good and should be changed somehow, because too many customers are unhappy about them.
quests.hint: A specific claim names the problem and the improvement.
quests.explanation: The best claim identifies the problem (surprise charges) and the fix. The others stay general.

quests.instruction: Choose the revision that replaces vague language with specifics.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The park needs some improvements.'
options: The park needs more benches and better lighting near the pond.
The park could benefit from some changes in general.
The park needs several important improvements in a number of areas.
The park needs to be improved in many different ways.
quests.hint: Vague words such as 'some' and 'improvements' should become concrete details.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence names what to add and where. The alternatives use vague words.

quests.instruction: Choose the most specific version.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The event went well.'
options: The event went very well overall, and people were happy.
The event drew 250 visitors and raised £1,800 for the school.
The event was quite successful in various respects and for many people.
The event was a positive experience for everyone involved.
quests.hint: Add numbers or facts.
quests.explanation: The best sentence gives numbers. The remaining options use positive but vague words.

quests.instruction: Which revision removes the vague phrase 'lots of reasons'?
quests.prompt: Original: 'There are lots of reasons why this policy is bad.'
options: There are many reasons why the policy is not good for us.
This policy is bad for several different reasons at once.
This policy has a number of negative points that matter.
This policy is unfair to part-time staff, and it adds paperwork for managers.
quests.hint: Name the reasons instead of counting them.
quests.explanation: The right revision states two actual reasons. The others still refer to reasons without naming them.

quests.instruction: Choose the best replacement for the weak topic sentence.
quests.prompt: Original topic sentence: 'Weekend markets are things.' The paragraph goes on to explain low fees, direct customer feedback and quick product testing.
options: There are many markets in a range of different places.
Weekend markets are held at the weekend in many towns.
Markets can be interesting for several different reasons.
Weekend markets give small businesses a low-risk way to test products.
quests.hint: The topic sentence should cover all the details that follow.
quests.explanation: The right sentence covers fees, feedback and testing. The remaining options are general or unrelated.

quests.instruction: Choose the best topic sentence.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Calendars are useful.' The paragraph explains that a shared calendar shows who is away, prevents double bookings and helps people plan around deadlines.
options: A shared calendar helps a team coordinate its time.
The shared calendar is used by our team every week.
Calendars have days and dates printed on them.
Calendars are used in many different workplaces.
quests.hint: The revision should reflect the paragraph's specific point.
quests.explanation: The best sentence covers absence, bookings and deadlines. The alternatives are general or describe.

quests.instruction: Which topic sentence best replaces 'This paragraph is about lunch breaks'?
quests.prompt: The paragraph explains that staff who take proper breaks return more focused.
options: Some staff take their lunch breaks at different times.
Lunch breaks are about having lunch in the middle of the day.
I will now explain what happens at lunch breaks.
Proper lunch breaks help staff return to work more focused.
quests.hint: State the point of the paragraph, not just its subject.
quests.explanation: This topic sentence makes a claim. The alternatives describe or announce.

quests.instruction: Which sentence should be cut from the paragraph?
quests.prompt: 'Free evening parking would help town-centre restaurants. Diners currently pay £6 to park after 6 p.m. Two owners said customers cancelled when they saw the charge. Several owners also complained about the price of ingredients.'
options: Free evening parking would help town-centre restaurants.
Several owners also complained about the price of ingredients.
Diners currently pay £6 to park after 6 p.m.
Two owners said customers cancelled when they saw the charge.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that does not support the parking argument.
quests.explanation: Ingredient prices are unrelated to parking. The other sentences support the argument.

quests.instruction: Which sentence should be removed?
quests.prompt: 'Schools should provide lockers. Heavy bags can strain students' backs. Lockers keep books and coats safe. The school also needs a new sports field.'
options: Heavy bags can strain students' backs.
Schools should provide lockers.
The school also needs a new sports field.
Lockers keep books and coats safe.
quests.hint: Ask which sentence does not relate to the locker argument.
quests.explanation: The sports field is a different issue. The other sentences support or state the locker claim.

quests.instruction: Which evidence should be cut because it does not support the claim?
quests.prompt: Claim: The library should offer free printing.
options: Printing job applications is often required.
Some families have no printer at home.
Many students cannot afford printing costs at home.
The library building was opened in 1972.
quests.hint: Which piece says nothing about the need for printing?
quests.explanation: The opening year does not show a need for free printing. The other statements show need.

quests.instruction: Choose the addition that best supports the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Most residents want a new playground.
options: A playground would be nice for the neighbourhood, and children in the flats would enjoy it a great deal.
Everyone I know agrees with this idea completely, and they would all be happy to see a playground built.
In a doorstep survey of 80 households, 61 said they would use a playground near the flats.
Playgrounds are places where children can play, run and meet friends, and they are found in most parks.
quests.hint: An unsupported claim needs evidence about residents' views.
quests.explanation: The survey figures show how many residents want a playground. The other options do not.

quests.instruction: Choose the best support.
quests.prompt: Claim: Remote meetings save time.
options: Time is valuable to everyone who works in an office, and nobody enjoys wasting it in a long meeting.
Last month our team saved about six hours of travel by joining the planning meeting online.
Many companies use remote meetings during the working week, and the number has grown over recent years.
Remote meetings are the future of work for most companies, and they will soon replace office meetings.
quests.hint: Look for a real measurement.
quests.explanation: The example gives a measurable saving. The remaining options are opinions or facts about use.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best supports the claim?
quests.prompt: Claim: The Mill Road route is dangerous for cyclists.
options: Cycling is a popular activity for many people, and more of them are riding to work than ever before.
Many roads are dangerous for people who ride bicycles, especially when the traffic is heavy at rush hour.
Three cyclists were hurt at the Mill Road junction last year, according to police records.
The route is really dangerous and cyclists know it well, so many of them avoid it at busy times.
quests.hint: Support should come from a record or observation about this route.
quests.explanation: Police records about this junction give direct evidence. The other choices assert, generalise or discuss cycling in general.

quests.instruction: Choose the revision that removes repetition.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The queue is long. The queue takes a lot of time. Waiting in the queue is slow.'
options: The queue is long, and the queue is slow, and waiting is slow.
The queue is long, the wait is long, and the time is long.
The long queue is long and slow, and the slow queue is time-consuming.
The queue is long and slow, so students lose much of their lunch break waiting.
quests.hint: Combine the repeated ideas and add what they mean for students.
quests.explanation: The right version merges three sentences into one and shows the effect. The rest still repeat.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Public toilets are important. They are needed by many people. Many people need public toilets every day.'
options: Public toilets are important, and many people need them, and they need them daily.
Public toilets serve thousands of daily visitors, including families and older people.
Many people need public toilets that people need every day.
Public toilets are important for people who need public toilets.
quests.hint: Replace repetition with specific information.
quests.explanation: This revision adds who uses toilets and how many. The remaining options repeat.

quests.instruction: Which revision removes repetition and keeps all the ideas?
quests.prompt: Original: 'Night shifts are tiring. Working at night makes people exhausted. Staff on night shifts need better breaks.'
options: Night shifts are exhausting, so staff working them need better breaks.
Night shifts are tiring. Staff need better breaks. Night shifts need better breaks.
Working at night is exhausting, and night workers are very tired.
Night shifts are tiring, exhausting and tiring, so staff need breaks.
quests.hint: Join the cause and the recommendation.
quests.explanation: This revision links exhaustion to the need for breaks. The others still repeat or lose the recommendation.

quests.instruction: Choose the smoothest, clearest rewrite.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The organisation of the meeting by the manager was done in a way that was not clear.'
options: The manager did the organisation of the meeting in a manner not clear.
The meeting's organisation was, by the manager, not made clear.
The manager organised the meeting unclearly.
The organisation of the meeting was unclear by the manager.
quests.hint: Use an active verb and cut unnecessary words.
quests.explanation: The best rewrite uses an active verb and is short. The others keep the awkward structure.

quests.instruction: Choose the best rewrite.
quests.prompt: Original: 'There are many students who are of the opinion that they should be given more time.'
options: Students, many of them, think they should be given time more.
There are many students who think that more time should be given to them.
Many students believe they should be given more time.
Many students are of the opinion that more time is a thing they should be given.
quests.hint: Remove 'there are' and 'of the opinion'.
quests.explanation: This version is short and direct. The others keep wordy or awkward structures.

quests.instruction: Choose the best rewrite.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Due to the fact that the bus was late, arrival at the office was late as well.'
options: Owing to the lateness of the bus, lateness occurred on arrival.
Because of the fact that the bus was late, arrival was also late.
As the bus was late, the arriving was late too.
The bus was late, so I arrived late.
quests.hint: Cut 'due to the fact that' and repeated words.
quests.explanation: The best version is simple and clear. The remaining options remain wordy.

quests.instruction: Choose the revision that keeps the concern but removes the anger.
quests.prompt: Original: 'This disgusting new fee is a slap in the face to every hardworking student!'
options: This unfair new fee is a real insult to hardworking students, and it should be dropped straight away.
The fee is a disaster for students everywhere, and it will make life much harder for every one of them.
The new fee places an extra cost on students who already work to cover their expenses.
This terrible fee is upsetting, and students hate it, so the college should think again about its decision.
quests.hint: Replace insults with a reason.
quests.explanation: The best revision explains why the fee is a problem. The rest still use emotional words.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Our shameful, heartless council has abandoned the town's children.'
options: The council's decision to close the youth centre leaves children with fewer places to go after school.
The council has shamefully closed the youth centre, and it should be made to explain why it did so.
The council does not care about the town's children, and it has shown that by closing the youth centre.
The council's cruel decision to close the youth centre abandons children and leaves them with nothing.
quests.hint: State what happened and its effect.
quests.explanation: The best revision reports the decision and its effect. The other choices keep accusations.

quests.instruction: Which revision keeps the concern but removes the anger?
quests.prompt: Original: 'I am absolutely furious that nobody bothered to fix the broken lift!'
options: The lift has been broken for two weeks, which makes it hard for wheelchair users to reach the second floor.
The broken lift shows how little this office cares about the people who work here or visit the building.
I am extremely upset that the broken lift has still not been fixed, after all of the complaints that were made.
It is disgraceful that nobody has fixed the lift, and I think the people responsible should be embarrassed.
quests.hint: Show the effect on people rather than the writer's feelings.
quests.explanation: The right revision gives the duration and the effect. The others remain emotional or accusatory.

quests.instruction: Choose the most accurate revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'All online classes are a waste of time.'
options: Online classes are almost always a waste of time.
Online classes are pretty much useless in every subject.
Online classes can be less effective for subjects that need hands-on practice.
Most online classes are a waste of time.
quests.hint: Replace 'all' with a limited, specific claim.
quests.explanation: The best revision limits the claim to a certain type of subject. The alternatives still condemn nearly all classes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Nobody reads long emails.'
options: Almost nobody reads long emails to the end, so writers should keep every message as short as possible.
Many people skim long emails, so key points should come first.
Very few people ever read long emails, and those who do are usually looking for a mistake.
People never read long emails properly, so anything important should be sent in a separate message.
quests.hint: Replace 'nobody' with a fair statement and add a consequence.
quests.explanation: This revision is accurate and gives advice. The alternatives remain extreme.

quests.instruction: Choose the most accurate revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Public transport is always better than driving.'
options: Public transport is generally better than driving everywhere.
Public transport is nearly always better than driving.
In busy city centres, public transport is often faster and cheaper than driving.
Driving is rarely a good option anywhere.
quests.hint: Specify where and how the claim is true.
quests.explanation: The right revision names the place and the qualities. The others still generalise.

quests.instruction: What is the main problem with the paragraph?
quests.prompt: 'Team lunches are great. They are great for teams. Everyone loves them. Nobody has ever disliked one.'
options: It ends with a conclusion that adds a new idea.
It uses a tone that is far too formal.
It makes broad claims and repeats them without evidence.
It gives too many facts and numbers.
quests.hint: Look at what is repeated and what is missing.
quests.explanation: The paragraph repeats 'great' and generalises without evidence. It has no numbers or new ideas.

quests.instruction: What is the main problem?
quests.prompt: 'We should ban homework. Homework is stupid, and teachers who set it are lazy.'
options: It has too many transitions, which makes the paragraph hard to follow from one sentence to the next.
It uses hedging language too often, so the reader cannot tell what the writer really thinks.
It gives too much evidence for its claim, so the reader has no space to form their own view.
It attacks people and uses insulting language instead of reasons.
quests.hint: Look for what the paragraph offers as support.
quests.explanation: The paragraph insults teachers rather than giving reasons. It has no evidence or hedges.

quests.instruction: What is the main problem?
quests.prompt: 'The new parking rules are unfair. The rules are unfair to drivers. Many drivers think the rules are unfair. Unfair rules should be changed.'
options: It has no topic sentence.
It is too balanced and considers both sides.
It gives an irrelevant example.
It repeats its claim without giving any reasons.
quests.hint: Count how many times the same idea appears.
quests.explanation: Every sentence repeats 'unfair'. The paragraph never explains why.
